claim: The demo queues user messages sent during model streaming and processes them after the current response completes.
An interrupt event stops consumption of the active model stream and returns the user to a state where another message can be sent.
Frontend input should not directly invoke a linear agent loop when the interaction must remain interruptible.
Model output, parsers, tool calls, and users can all contribute events that other services observe.
The proposed state model makes current state a pure function of the events that occurred instead of a separately synchronized mutable object.
Different renderings can be projected from the same event sequence, including queued messages, interruptions, partial streams, and forks.
Replaying events makes UI states testable without manually coordinating a running frontend and backend.
The demonstrated backend uses an event bus whose services subscribe to events and may publish additional events.
